newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai refiners' margins cushioned by local market.
newsitem.headline: Thai refiners' margins cushioned by local market.

text.p: Thailand's oil refineries are comfortable with the current weak state of profit margins and unlikely to follow the course of Singapore refiners and cut production, sources at the refineries said on Thursday.
For the time being, Thai refiners can rely on support from the domestic market -- which absorbs almost all of their 760,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) output, the sources said.
"We are not considering a production cut -- this level for margins is okay," said a source at the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), which partly owns four of Thailand's five refineries.
Thailand is one of the few oil markets in Asia that has been deregulated, so its refiners are very sensitive to international price swings.
But selling prices to domestic markets are sufficient to keep margins positive, unlike in Singapore -- Asia's bellwether refining centre.
Singapore refiners have been losing about 50 cents per barrel on basic refining since mid-May, compared to profits of more than $2.00 in April.
The losses prompted Exxon Corp to cut output at its 230,000 bpd refinery by 10 percent. Traders said Singapore's three other refineries were expected to follow suit.
Most of Singapore's 1.3 million bpd output is exported, so the refineries have to rely on international prices to find their profit margins.
While margins for Thailand's refining sector are positive, they have fallen.
"We have to monitor the margins very closely," said a source at refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc.
He said the refinery's refining margins for the production of premium products have dropped to just over $2.00 per barrel, compared to a normal range of $2.50-$3.00.

"The hydro-skimming yield is much lower than normal but it is still higher than our variable costs," he said. "The retail margin is not as bad as the refining margin...it's not much better, but that's why refiners are able to survive."

"It is different for Singapore," another refiner said. "In Thailand, a lot of product is consumed domestically and product prices are on a c&f (cost-and-freight delivered) basis which is higher than Singapore...it helps."
Thailand's consumption of refined products averaged 747,190 bpd in the first quarter of 1997. That shows that 98 percent of Thailand's refinery output is bought by the domestic market.
The domestic cushion allowed Thailand to avoid making production cuts in January, when Singapore refiners cut runs because of weak international price margins.
